title: Proper and Zariski normal form of an arbitrary ordinary alteration cover
statement: Let $X$ be a nonempty integral quasi-excellent Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $(T_b\to X)_{b\in B}$ be any finite covering family in the ordinary alteration topology [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology]. There are a nonempty integral Noetherian scheme $P$, a proper surjective morphism $g:P\to X$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism] with finite function-field extension $k(P)/k(X)$, a finite Zariski open cover $P=\bigcup_{j\in J}P_j$ [def-weil-open-immersion], indices $b(j)\in B$, and $X$-morphisms $P_j\to T_{b(j)}$. The function field of an integral scheme is its local ring at its unique generic point. No regularity of the $T_b$ or of $P$ is assumed or concluded, and no prime-to-a-prime degree constraint is imposed.

source.place: Expose II Theorem 3.2.1 and its proof in the ordinary case (parameter 1), printed p.29; finite extraction from the open cover by quasi-compactness of the proper Noetherian source. This is a theorem about arbitrary ordinary alteration covers, not about regular uniformization.

proof.text: Work on $\mathcal C=\operatorname{alt}/X$ of [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology]. Every object is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and has finite fibres over generic points of $X$ by [lem-per-generic-fibre-finiteness-criterion]. Every arrow $A\to T$ in $\mathcal C$ sends component-generic points to component-generic points: a generic point of $A$ maps into a finite generic fibre of $T/X$, whose points admit no proper specializations inside that fibre; any component-generic generalization of its image also lies in that fibre. The residue extension for $A/T$ is an intermediate extension of the finite one for $A/X$. The arrow is of finite type: on affine charts its algebra is generated over the target algebra by its generators over the base, and preimages of affine opens are quasi-compact: [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space] makes each chart in a finite Noetherian affine cover a Noetherian space; every open in their finite union is quasi-compact. Thus an arrow of $\mathcal C$ makes its source an object of $\operatorname{alt}/T$.

Fibre products in $\mathcal C$ are the dominant reduced parts of ordinary scheme fibre products. Indeed [lem-per-dominant-part-coreflection] gives their universal property for reduced maximally dominant test schemes. They remain objects: over a generic point of $X$, a product of finite schemes is finite, since the tensor algebra is spanned by the tensors of two finite bases; reduction is a quotient and remains finite. Finite type is preserved by base change and composition by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. The same calculation, using Step 1 over a component-generic point of $T$, proves finiteness of generic fibres after pulling back any arrow along $T'\to T$ in $\mathcal C$.

For each $T$ in $\mathcal C$, let $K(T)$ consist of presieves admitting a refinement $(V_a\hookrightarrow Y\to T)_{a\in A}$, where $Y\to T$ is a proper surjection in $\mathcal C$ and the $V_a$ form a finite open cover of $Y$. Isomorphism presieves belong to $K$ using $Y=T$ and the single open $T$. Pull back a witness along $T'\to T$. Its ordinary proper map stays proper and surjective by [lem-pc-proper-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]; taking dominant reduced parts preserves these properties by [lem-per-dominant-part-coreflection]; the dominant reduced part of $T'$ is $T'$ itself, since $T'$ is reduced and all its component-generic points lie over generic points of $X$. Pulling back each open gives an open cover of the ordinary product, and restricting it to the dominant reduced part still covers. Its pieces equal the categorical pullbacks: open immersions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], so the etale comparison in the coreflection identifies them. The factorization maps of the witness pull back functorially. Thus $K$ has pullbacks and is stable under base change.

To check composition for $K$, take a witness $(V_a\hookrightarrow Y\xrightarrow{p}T)_a$ for a first presieve $R$, with each $V_a\to T$ factoring through an arrow $A_a\to T$ of $R$. For a $K$-covering presieve on every such $A_a$, pull its witness to $V_a$ by Step 3. Write it as a proper surjection $Q_a\to V_a$ followed by a finite open cover $(W_{ac})_c$ of $Q_a$. Apply [lem-per-zariski-proper-surjection-interchange] over $Y$ to the cover $(V_a)_a$ and these $Q_a$. Step 1 and composition of finite type show that $Q_a\to Y$ is in $\operatorname{alt}/Y$, so the lemma applies. Obtain $Z\to Y$ proper surjective with maps $Z\times_YV_a\to Q_a$. Then $Z$ is an object of $\mathcal C$: $Z\to X$ is of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], $Z$ is reduced, and a component-generic point of $Z$ maps to one of $Y$ and then to a generic point of $X$, with residue extension the composite of two finite extensions. The inverse images of $W_{ac}$ under these maps form a finite open cover of $Z$, with maps into the required composite presieve. The composite $Z\to Y\to T$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] and surjective because both maps are. This proves composition stability of $K$.

source.place: II 3.2.1, ordinary-case proof, p.29, exchange of an open cover and proper maps over its members.

proof.text: Let $J$ be the ordinary alteration topology. Every $K$-witness is a composite of a proper surjective generator and a Zariski cover; the latter is an etale generator by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Thus $J$ contains the sieves generated by $K$. Conversely a proper surjective generator belongs to $K$ by taking its whole source as one open. For any jointly surjective etale generator, apply [lem-per-etale-cover-finite-zariski-refinement] to its reduced Noetherian target. It supplies a finite surjection and a finite open cover refining that generator; the finite map is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. All schemes and maps stay in $\mathcal C$: the lemma gives an object over the target and Step 1 gives finite generic residue extensions, which remain finite on composition. Hence each generator of $J$ belongs to $K$. By the two minimality properties, the topology generated by $K$ is exactly $J$.

Let $R$ be the sieve generated by the given $(T_b\to X)_{b\in B}$. It is $J$-covering by hypothesis. Apply [lem-per-generated-precoverage-covering-sieve] to $K$: isomorphisms, pullbacks and composition were verified in Steps 3--4. By Step 5 its generated topology is $J$. Therefore $R$ contains a presieve in $K(X)$. Its witness gives a proper surjection $q:Q\to X$ in $\mathcal C$, a finite open cover $(V_a)_a$ of $Q$, and maps from the $V_a$ into arrows of $R$. Each such arrow factors through some $T_b$ by the definition of generated sieve. Composing gives $X$-maps $V_a\to T_{b(a)}$.

proof.text: Choose a point of $Q$ over the generic point $\eta$ of $X$, which exists since $q$ is surjective, and a component containing it by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover]. The component has a unique generic point by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]; its image generalizes $\eta$, hence is $\eta$. Give the component its reduced induced closed structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], and call it $P$. It is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Its map $g:P\to X$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. The image is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image] and contains $\eta$, so it is all of $X$. Properness includes finite type, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $P$ Noetherian. Its generic point is a component-generic point of the object $Q$, and the reduced closed immersion preserves its residue field (on an affine chart both residue fields are the fraction field of the same prime quotient), so [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology] gives the finite extension $k(P)/k(X)$.

source.place: II 3.2.1, end of ordinary-case proof: if X is irreducible choose an integral source; Stacks 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober), 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian).

proof.text: Put $P_a=P\times_QV_a$, the inverse-image open subschemes. They form a finite open cover of $P$ since the $V_a$ cover $Q$. Restrict the maps $V_a\to T_{b(a)}$ to obtain $P_a\to T_{b(a)}$. Their composites to $X$ are $g|_{P_a}$ because every map used was over $X$. Discard empty opens if desired. The nonempty scheme $P$ ensures at least one open remains. These maps and the proper integral surjection of Step 7 give all clauses; no regularity or degree-coprimality assertion has been used.
